html:
The Wiriyamu massacre took place on 16 December 1972, when Portuguese troops killed about 400 villagers in Wiriyamu and nearby villages in Tete province, Mozambique, suspected of helping FRELIMO guerrillas.

Soldiers rounded up the people, many of them women and children, and shot them or burned them in their huts. Catholic missionaries collected the names of the dead.

The British priest Adrian Hastings made it public in The Times of London in July 1973, just before a state visit to Britain by the Portuguese prime minister. The news caused an international scandal and weakened support for Portugal's wars, shortly before the Carnation Revolution. It became a symbol of the war of independence.
sum: The Wiriyamu massacre took place on 16 December 1972, when Portuguese troops killed about 400 villagers in Wiriyamu and nearby villages in Tete province, Mozambique, suspected of helping FRELIMO guerrillas.
